To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
learning to cross boundaries is an essential process to make an integrated care network work.
learning to cross boundaries requires a process of collective reflection and action in which social contact, direct interaction, and shared experiences play a key role.

through a process of social learning, health professionals learned how to cross professional and organisational boundary to make sure patients received the right care, in the right moment, at the right place.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how health care providers learn to cross the boundaries that exist between them to deliver seamless care.
how professionals learn to integrate their work, how they cross boundaries and how they create the conditions to do so.
the development of the network as a social system and the development of the individual health professional as a network professional.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
through learning to cross boundaries, the network was able to develop and implement a shared vision and a shared language, to improve the coordination of care for the patients.
learning is an essential element of boundary crossing in integrated care.

the development of an interprofessional network of health care professionals is an evolutionary learning process in which the development of social contacts between health care professionals is essential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of an effective network depends not only on the development of the network itself, but on the development of its members.
through a process of learning and unlearning, professionals were enabled to cross the boundaries of the professional and organisatory context and to work together to provide seamless care.
the development of integrated care is a process of collective and experiential learning, in which social contacts between professionals and organisations are important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of health care networks requires more than a change in structures, procedures and protocols; it also requires a change of perspective.
learning is not a linear, but a cyclical process, in which professionals learn from their experience and from each other.
it is important to provide time, space and support for care givers to learn to work in an integrated network.
